Eli: Hi all, newbie here. About to open my first PR touching the router and a tiny unit test. Quick checklist: preferred branch pattern, commit style, and how strict are PR size expectations?

Mar: Welcome Eli! We like `feat/<TICKET>-short-desc` or `fix/<TICKET>-short-desc`. Keep changes atomic. If it's purely runtime logic + its test, a single PR is fine. If it changes public config or schemas, split into generator/schema PR then callers.

Riley: PR size guidance: try to keep functional code under ~350 LOC. Tests can inflate that; note in the PR body if test fixtures make it large. If it's >700 LOC, add a short justification.

Eli: Cool. Commit messages? Squash?

Mar: Use `area(scope): brief summary` e.g., `runtime(router): simplify route lookup`. Squash on merge for small fixes; preserve history for multi-part features.

Eli: Pre-commit / CI checks? My formatter complains.

ci-bot: Repo hooks: black, isort, flake8, mypy. CI will block merges on failing hooks. Run `pre-commit run --all-files` or `make dev-setup` to install hooks. See CI: https://ci.redwood.example/job/1755559999

Riley: We also have `scripts/autoformat.sh` for quick fixes. If CI is flaky, add `flake` label and ping @eng-oncall.

Eli: Reviewers and labels?

devx: Add 2 reviewers: one CODEOWNER for the touched directory + one peer. Labels: `area/runtime`, `needs-review`. If it's latency sensitive add `needs-perf` and mention @Riley. Include a brief rollout and rollback plan in the PR body.

Mar: Example rollback text: "Rollback: revert PR -> redeploy service -> invalidate route cache: `tools/cachectl purge --prefix=router:`". Also include a simple test plan (commands to run locally).

Eli: Any other gotchas? Generated files, binaries?

Riley: Don't commit generated outputs (gen/) unless you updated the generator. Run `scripts/generate.sh` locally before pushing if you touched schema files. Use `git add -p` to avoid large accidental diffs.

Eli: Thanks, will open and paste the PR link here. Appreciate the help! :pray:
